input.sha256_scope: No input pixels are committed, so this is a digest over the six per-record `source_rgb_sha256` values in expected.json, concatenated in record order. Every case is a deterministic synthetic image generated by the closed form (x*7 + y*13 + c*29) % 256, reproduced identically in the capture tool and the Rust test; the test checks each record's own hash, and this value summarises the set so a changed or reordered case is visible in one place.
input.provenance: Generated by formula. Two cases are around a megapixel and exist only to land on a rounding boundary, which is why a closed form was used rather than committed pixels.

upstream.capture_method: The pinned PaddleX operators were imported and executed, not transcribed. Earlier captures reimplemented the upstream operators inside the capture tool; this one calls ResizeByShort, Crop, Normalize, ToCHWImage, ToBatch, and Topk themselves, so a transcription error is not among the ways it can be wrong.

limitations: The model is never run. Scores are synthetic, so this fixture pins preprocessing and postprocessing exactly and says nothing about the model's accuracy.
Tensors are compared by sha256 over all 150,528 values plus 256 evenly spaced samples. The samples exist to make a failure readable; the hash is the claim.
Two cases sit on the round-half-to-even boundary of ResizeByShort. They are the only cases where the PaddleX baseline and the C++ baseline disagree, and they are captured for exactly that reason.

`artifacts` is null on purpose: the repository gate reserves that field for reviewed end-to-end fixtures that load a model, and this fixture loads none. The artifact's identity and hashes are recorded under `artifact_provenance` and in docs/TABLE_CLASSIFICATION_CONTRACT.md.

artifact_provenance.used_by_the_capture: Only for its hashes and its config. No inference session was created: the input tensor and the Topk postprocess are the whole compatibility surface here, and Topk is fully determined by the score vector handed to it.
